title: Fix changelog generator edge case: deterministic ordering for same-day metadata events
author: Michael Nguyen
description: Problem: The changelog generator collapses multiple metadata update events that occur on the same calendar day into a single draft entry in some cases. We saw this in staging when a model version received two back-to-back updates (compatibility matrix + deprecation messaging) and the later event overwrote/merged the earlier one depending on iteration order. Root cause: the aggregation key for draft rendering used (model_id, version_id, yyyy-mm-dd) and then iterated over the day-bucketed events without a deterministic sort, so output depended on upstream fetch order and Go map iteration. Fix: introduce deterministic ordering by event_id (lexicographic, since event_id is a ULID-like identifier emitted by the registry) and stop using day as the primary key for collapsing; instead we generate a stable per-event "change_group_id" for rendering while still allowing the UI to show a same-day grouping. This preserves multiple distinct changes within a day and makes the generator idempotent across reruns. Also adds regression tests and a backfill-safe guard so existing published entries are not re-keyed. Notes: This does not change public feed pagination semantics; it only affects draft rendering and how we compute the per-entry ordering within a given model/version timeline. Follow-up: we should consider explicitly surfacing "event_count" in the entry metadata for the Console compare view (tracked separately).
commits: generator: sort event batches deterministically by event_id before rendering
generator: replace day-bucket collapse map with stable grouping + ordering
tests: add fixture with 3 same-day events and assert stable output ordering
metrics: add counter for same-day multi-event groups and log structured debug
snippet: Before: dayBuckets[dayKey] = append(dayBuckets[dayKey], e); for _, events := range dayBuckets { render(events) } // events order non-deterministic. After: sort.Slice(events, func(i,j int) bool { return events[i].EventID < events[j].EventID }); render(events) and write entry ordering_key = first_event_id (plus per-event sequence for same-day groups).
testing: Unit: services/model-changelog-generator/... (added regression test for same-day multi-event ordering). Integration (staging): reran generator on the failing staging model/version and verified 2 distinct draft sections were produced in deterministic order, and reruns are byte-for-byte identical.

review_conversation: Quentin Harris: Can we rely on event_id ordering being globally monotonic? Michael Nguyen: Yes; registry emits ULID-like IDs so lexicographic sort matches time order, but we still treat it as an ordering key not an absolute timestamp and keep created_at for display. Connor O'Brien: Does this change how release engineering expects "one entry per day"? Michael Nguyen: UI can still group by day; we’re only preventing overwrite/collapse at generation time and keeping multiple changes within the same date. Jada Williams: Please add a test that fails under non-deterministic iteration (simulate shuffled input). Michael Nguyen: Added fixture test with shuffled input and asserted stable output ordering and stable entry IDs. Logan Wright: Add a metric so we can see how often this happens in prod. release_notes: Internal: Fixes non-deterministic collapsing of same-day model metadata change events in changelog generator; ensures idempotent output ordering by event_id.
